judged_text: The update test asserts the revised content but never asserts that content_sha1 was persisted or that importing identical content skips the revision, leaving the new sha1-comparison branch half-verified. A regression in the content_sha1 update (topic_embed.rb:44 embed.update_column) or in the unchanged-content short-circuit (content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1) would pass this suite — e.g. if update_column were removed, every poll would silently rewrite the post and the tests would still be green; the 'import is idempotent' property the sha1 exists to provide is never asserted.

A regression in the content_sha1 update (topic_embed.rb:44 embed.update_column) or in the unchanged-content short-circuit (content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1) would pass this suite — e.g. if update_column were removed, every poll would silently rewrite the post and the tests would still be green; the 'import is idempotent' property the sha1 exists to provide is never asserted.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import` the sha1-based idempotency logic is new and nontrivial: it only revises the post when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` and then persists the new sha via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (topic_embed.rb around the update branch). The added spec `Supports updating the post` only asserts the post content changed (`post.cooked` matches /new contents/) and never asserts (a) `topic_embeds.content_sha1` was updated after a revision, nor (b) that re-importing identical `contents` does not call `PostRevisor` / does not rewrite the post. So a regression removing `update_column` or breaking the unchanged-content short-circuit could still leave tests green. This is a concrete missing-test gap rather than a demonstrated runtime defect in the diff.
